title: A Simple Way to Fix Wobbly Furniture Without Guessing
description: Find out whether the problem is an uneven floor, a short leg or a loose joint, then fix the actual cause instead of stacking random shims.
image_alt: Wooden furniture in a calm living room
body_html:
A chair, table or cabinet that rocks is annoying, but the fix is often small. The important part is identifying why it rocks before reaching for glue or a pile of folded cardboard.

First, find the movement

Place the furniture on its normal floor surface and gently press each corner. If the same corner repeatedly lifts, mark it. Then rotate the furniture 90 degrees and test again. If the rocking changes, the floor may be contributing to the problem.

Separate floor problems from furniture problems

Place a thin, temporary shim under the lifting corner. If the piece becomes stable, measure the shim thickness. If the furniture still twists or a joint moves, the structure itself needs attention.

For loose joints, fix the joint

Check screws, bolts and visible joints. Tighten hardware carefully without stripping it. For wooden joints that have separated, use the appropriate wood-repair method rather than forcing the piece back together under load.

For a small floor difference, use a proper solution

A purpose-made furniture pad or leveler is cleaner and more stable than improvised paper or cardboard. On valuable or heavy furniture, choose a solution that cannot slide out under normal use.

The final safety check

  • Test the furniture from several directions.
  • Make sure doors and drawers still open normally.
  • Check that the repair does not create a new tipping hazard.
  • Do not place heavy loads on a piece that still moves.

Good repairs start with diagnosis. If the movement comes from a structural crack, damaged fastener or unsafe load-bearing part, stop treating it as a simple wobble and repair the underlying damage.
